title: URLs form silently mis-parses bare URLs (no angle brackets)
description: RFC 8621 §4.1.2.7: 'Any value outside of the angle bracket arguments MUST be ignored.' Bare URLs like 'https://example.com/' (no <>) are spec-required to be ignored, but the implementation pipes them through mail_parser::MessageStream::parse_address. The address parser treats ':' as a group separator and '/' as token content, so 'https://example.com/u/abc' is parsed as group 'https' containing addresses '//example.com/u/abc'. The address field of those parsed addrs may then surface as a URL in HeaderValueTyped::URLs, violating the spec. Probe: assert_eq!(parse_header_typed(HeaderForm::URLs, b"https://example.com/u/abc"), HeaderValueTyped::URLs(vec![])) — expected to fail today; expected actual is some garbage list. Fix: pre-scan raw bytes for <...>-delimited URL substrings and only feed those to the address parser, OR write a small dedicated <URL> tokenizer in this module.
close_reason: Fixed: URLs form now uses a dedicated RFC 2369 bracket tokenizer rather than mail-parser's address parser. Bare URLs (no <...> framing) produce empty result per RFC 8621 §4.1.2.7. URLs containing commas, colons (tel:, https:), and CRLF folding artifacts are now handled correctly. Contract is mime-tree's own, not delegated.
